title: System Design for Software Development
content: System design involves not just writing code, but deciding how all the pieces of the system should work together. An analogy for understanding system design is designing a city. Writing code is like constructing individual buildings. System design is about deciding where roads should go, where electricity should come from, how traffic should work, where hospitals should be located, and how the city should grow. A city with beautiful buildings but poor infrastructure will fail. Similarly, software can have beautifully written code, but if the architecture cannot handle growth or failures, it will also fail.

System design is deciding where should the roads go, where should electricity come from, how should traffic work, where should hospitals are located, What happens if one road gets blocked?
